title: The Invisible Web: The Geopolitics of Global Subsea Internet Cables
subtitle: Understanding the physical infrastructure that powers the global digital economy and national security.
description: Over 99% of international data traffic travels through subsea cables, yet this infrastructure remains largely invisible to the public. This series explores how these critical connections have become a focal point of geopolitical competition, national security concerns, and global economic strategy.

articles.label: Part 1
articles.note: Establishing the physical reality of the internet versus the myth of 'the cloud'.

articles.label: Part 2
articles.note: The shift from telecommunications consortia to private tech giants (Google, Meta, Amazon) owning the infrastructure.

articles.label: Part 3
articles.note: The vulnerability of cables to physical sabotage and state-level espionage.

articles.label: Part 4
articles.note: Taiwan as a critical hub in the Indo-Pacific cable network and the challenges of maintaining connectivity.

articles.label: Part 5
articles.note: How governments and companies are building redundancy and resilience into the global network.
